designs.title: Pisa
designs.why: Clean, confident one-ink line work that prints easily and reads as Pisa instantly; the stamp format and the '3.97°' denomination (the tower's real lean) give it a smart, giftable souvenir feel, and it works on both white and black. But the gag of an upright tower in a tilted stamp reads on a hanger or across a store as a crooked print rather than a joke, so returns and 'is this misprinted?' questions are a real risk. The scattered grass tufts and dashed road are weak filler next to the detailed tower, and at this size the 3.97° clue is too small to explain the idea.
designs.fix: Make the joke impossible to miss: keep the stamp square to the shirt and let the tower itself lean the 3.97°, or give the denomination and lean more prominence (e.g., a bigger '3.97°' with a small angle arc at the base), so the tilt reads as intentional and not as a misplaced print.
